highlights.title: SoftBank Draws Over $20 Billion of Early Interest in Junk Bond
highlights.description: SoftBank Group Corp. has drawn more than $20 billion of preliminary demand for what’s shaping up to be one of the biggest junk bond deals ever, people familiar with the matter said, as investors rush to capture record yields likely to be offered to help fund the firm’s investments in OpenAI.

business.title: Rising Yields Pose Risk to Equity Valuations, RBC BlueBay Says
business.description: Mike Bell, head of market strategy at RBC BlueBay Asset Management, discusses the outlook for bond yields, equity valuations and the artificial intelligence trade. "The equity risk premium is very compressed," Bell says on Bloomberg Television. "Any moves higher in bond yields are going to push that earnings yield up and therefore valuations on stocks down," he adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: Northern Trust Co-CIO Says 'Buy More Stocks' on Valuations
business.description: Anwiti Bahuguna, global co-chief investment officer at Northern Trust Asset Management, discusses the artificial intelligence trade, and says US stocks are undervalued based on the earnings picture. "You buy more stocks in that environment," she tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: AI Cloud Startup Verda Raises $189 Million in Funding Round

business.title: VeriSilicon CEO on Business Strategy
business.description: Wayne Dai, Chairman, CEO and President of Shanghai listed chip-design firm VeriSilicon, discusses his company's business and growth strategy, as it looks to expand to more markets globally. He speaks with Shery Ahn on the sidelines of CITIC Securities’ International Investors’ Forum on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

As previously reported, the feature will use the gyroscope, accelerometer, and other sensors to determine when an iPhone has been grabbed. devices.title: Apple Quietly Excludes Older iPhones From New Camera Feature
devices.description: Apple's new Texture and Grain controls for Photographic Styles are not available on iPhones other than the latest iPhone 18 Pro models and upcoming iPhone Duo, despite the company's original wording suggesting otherwise. When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max earlier this month, its Newsroom press release said the new Texture and Grain controls would be "available in iOS 27 on iPhone models that support the latest generation of Photographic Styles."
